scenarios.name: write-new-record
scenarios.why: a new key: WRITE NORMAL, then GET-ME-OUT-OF-HERE's RETURN; the record is the 681-byte COMMAREA

scenarios.name: same-utime-other-task
scenarios.why: the UTIME part of an existing key with another task number: a different key, NORMAL

scenarios.name: duplicate-key

commarea.ABND-FREEFORM: a second abend in the same task and microsecond

scenarios.why: the key exists: WRITE DUPREC (RESP 14) -> the DISPLAYs and RETURN; the file is unchanged

scenarios.name: negative-codes
scenarios.why: SIGN LEADING SEPARATE fields negative, at their 8-digit limit; task number 9999 (PIC 9(4) maximum)

scenarios.name: key-zero
scenarios.why: boundary: UTIME 0 and task 0, the lowest key

scenarios.name: key-max
scenarios.why: boundary: UTIME 999999999999999 (S9(15) COMP-3 maximum), task 9999, the free-form text filled to 600 bytes

scenarios.name: write-nospace

faults.why: 18 on the WRITE -> the 'Unable to write' DISPLAYs and RETURN

scenarios.why: injected NOSPACE: the error path, nothing written

notes: CBSA's abend recorder (ABNDPROC, LINKed by the other CBSA programs with an ABNDINFO-shaped COMMAREA): MOVE DFHCOMMAREA TO WS-ABND-AREA, EXEC CICS WRITE FILE('ABNDFILE') FROM(WS-ABND-AREA) RIDFLD(ABND-VSAM-KEY) RESP RESP2; on a non-NORMAL RESP it DISPLAYs 'Unable to write to the file ABNDFILE' with the RESP / RESP2 and RETURNs, else RETURNs through GET-ME-OUT-OF-HERE. DUPREC is exercised naturally (an existing key), NOSPACE / NOTOPEN by fault injection. The COMMAREA is described as BNKMENU's ABNDINFO-REC (the ABND-* names): the contract DTO the generator gives ABNDPROC is that caller's record -- the same 681-byte ABNDINFO layout ABNDPROC's own DFHCOMMAREA has as COMM-*. The DISPLAY lines go to the COBOL task's stdout, which the CICS harness does not compare: only the events (RETURN) and the file are compared. Each scenario's ABNDFILE is compared after the task. Keys: ABND-VSAM-KEY is ABND-UTIME-KEY PIC S9(15) COMP-3 (8 bytes) + ABND-TASKNO-KEY PIC 9(4): binary packed bytes then digits, no letters possible from the COMMAREA's numeric fields; no browse, so no key order is exercised. ABND-RESPCODE / RESP2CODE / SQLCODE are SIGN LEADING SEPARATE (9 bytes each). The CICS file's DSNAME CBSA.CICSBSA.ABNDFILE is joined to the IDCAMS define @BANK_PREFIX@.ABNDFILE (KEYS(12 0), RECORDSIZE 681) by the engine's symbolic candidate join (#3656). Data: abndfile.bin is SYNTHETIC (three abend records, the corpus ships none), fixed 681-byte ABNDINFO records one per line, with packed keys chosen so that no byte is a line end.
